# Rflap MCP tools

<!-- Generated by `rflap-mcp --tools-markdown`; a test keeps this file in sync. -->

Every tool answers with `content` (Markdown for chats without the widget) and, when it succeeds, `structuredContent` (the Rflap API result; visual tools add `tool` and, when they have one, `document`). A failure is a result with `isError: true` and the API's error code and message, never a JSON-RPC error. Tools marked *shows the widget* carry `_meta.ui.resourceUri = "ui://rflap/editor.html"`.

## `rflap_design_automaton`

**Design an automaton from a language** · shows the widget

Builds, minimizes and VERIFIES an automaton for a language you have already reasoned out. You translate the student's language into a formal spec; Rflap builds the minimal DFA (or a PDA for a non-regular template), draws it and checks it against your examples and against a brute-force cross-check. Give the alphabet, exactly ONE of constraint_text / constraint / regex / grammar / template, and accept/reject examples (include the empty string and boundary cases). If the verification reports a failing example, your spec or example is wrong: fix it and call again. constraint_text syntax: starts_with("ab"), ends_with("ab"), contains("aa"), length >= 3, length % 2 == 0, count(a) % 2 == 0, count(a,b) >= 2 (a or b), count(a) == count(b) (NOT regular), regex("(a+b)*"), combined with and / or / xor / not and parentheses. Regex syntax is JFLAP's: + union, * star, juxtaposition concatenation, λ empty string. Non-regular languages need a template. Example: {"alphabet":"ab","constraint_text":"ends_with(\"ab\")","examples":{"accept":["ab","aab"],"reject":["","ba","abb"]}}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alphabet` | string or array of string | yes | The symbols, single characters: "ab" or ["a","b"]. |
| `constraint` | object | no | A structured condition: {"type":"ends_with","word":"ab"}, starts_with, contains, length {cmp,n}, length_mod {m,r}, count {symbols,cmp,n}, count_mod {symbols,m,r}, regex {pattern}, and/or/xor {constraints:[...]}, not {constraint}. Prefer constraint_text. |
| `constraint_text` | string | no | A condition in text syntax, e.g. ends_with("ab") and count(a) % 2 == 0. |
| `examples` | object | no | Strings the automaton must accept and reject ("" is the empty string). |
| `grammar` | string | no | The language as a right- or left-linear grammar, one production per line: "S -> aS \| bA". |
| `options` | object | no | Optional: check_len (brute-force length, default 8), layout (circle, gem, spiral, tree, ...), include_trap_state (default true). |
| `regex` | string | no | The language as a regular expression (JFLAP syntax). |
| `template` | object | no | A non-regular language, built as a PDA: {"name":"an_bn","a":"a","b":"b","min":0}, {"name":"an_bm","a":"a","b":"b","relation":"le"\|"ge"\|"ne"}, {"name":"equal_count","a":"a","b":"b"}, {"name":"balanced_brackets","pairs":[["(",")"]]}, {"name":"wcwr","c":"c"}, {"name":"even_palindrome"}, {"name":"palindrome"}. |

`structuredContent` keys: `description`, `document`, `states`, `verification`.

## `rflap_show`

**Show a document** · shows the widget

Shows any Rflap document (automaton, grammar, regex, L-system…) in the interactive widget and returns its analysis (deterministic?, unreachable states…), a transition table and an explanation. Use it to display something you wrote by hand. Example: {"document":{"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"],"transitions":[["q0","a","q1"],["q1","b","q0"]]}}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | object | yes | The document to show. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |

`structuredContent` keys: `analysis`, `document`, `explanation`, `svg`.

## `rflap_simulate`

**Simulate a machine on inputs** · shows the widget

Runs a finite automaton, PDA, Turing machine, Mealy or Moore machine on one input (`input`) or on many (`inputs`, a batch table). Returns accepted / rejected / undecided and the trace of configurations. Options: mode step_by_state|closure (λ handling), acceptance final_state|empty_stack (PDA) or final_state|halting|both (Turing), `tapes` for one string per tape of a multi-tape machine. Example: {"document":{"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"],"transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]},"input":"a"}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acceptance` | `final_state` \| `empty_stack` \| `halting` \| `both` | no | When a run accepts (PDA, Turing). |
| `document` | object | yes | The machine to run. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `input` | string | no | One input string ("" is the empty string). |
| `inputs` | array of string or array of string | no | Many inputs at once (a batch run); each a string, or an array with one string per tape. |
| `max_configs` | integer | no | Configurations explored before answering undecided (default 10000). |
| `mode` | `step_by_state` \| `closure` | no | How λ transitions are stepped. |
| `tapes` | array of string | no | One input per tape of a multi-tape Turing machine (single run). |

`structuredContent` keys: `accepted`, `document`, `outcome`, `results`, `trace`.

## `rflap_step`

**Step through a run** · shows the widget

Runs an input for exactly `steps` steps (stateless: it replays from the start) and returns the live configurations (`frontier`), those already accepted or rejected, and whether the run finished. Call it with steps 1, 2, 3… to walk a student through a run; the widget highlights the current states. Example: {"document":{...},"input":"aab","steps":2}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acceptance` | `final_state` \| `empty_stack` \| `halting` \| `both` | no | When a run accepts (PDA, Turing). |
| `document` | object | yes | The machine to run. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `input` | string | yes | The input string. |
| `max_configs` | integer | no | Frontier size at which the run stops as truncated (default 10000). |
| `mode` | `step_by_state` \| `closure` | no | How λ transitions are stepped. |
| `steps` | integer | no | Steps to take from the start (default 1). |
| `tapes` | array of string | no | One input per tape of a multi-tape Turing machine. |

`structuredContent` keys: `document`, `finished`, `frontier`, `steps_done`.

## `rflap_convert`

**Convert between models** · shows the widget

Converts a document. Targets (`to`): dfa, minimal_dfa (from fa, regex or regular grammar); regex, regular_grammar (from fa); nfa (from regex); fa (from a right-linear grammar); pda_ll, pda_lr (from a CFG); cfg (from a pda); unrestricted_grammar (from a one-tape Turing machine); remove_lambda, remove_unit, remove_useless, cnf (grammar transformations); complete (adds the trap state), split_labels, remove_useless_states. Returns the new document and the construction steps. Example: {"document":{"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"},"to":"minimal_dfa"}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | object | yes | The document to convert. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `to` | `dfa` \| `minimal_dfa` \| `regex` \| `nfa` \| `regular_grammar` \| `fa` \| `pda_ll` \| `pda_lr` \| `cfg` \| `unrestricted_grammar` \| `remove_lambda` \| `remove_unit` \| `remove_useless` \| `cnf` \| `complete` \| `split_labels` \| `remove_useless_states` | yes | The target. |

`structuredContent` keys: `document`, `steps`, `to`.

## `rflap_equivalent`

**Compare two languages**

Whether two finite automata, regular expressions or right-linear grammars accept the same language; when they do not, a shortest counterexample string. Use it to check a student's automaton against a regex. Example: {"a":{"type":"fa",...},"b":{"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*ab"}}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | object | yes | The first language. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `b` | object | yes | The second language. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |

`structuredContent` keys: `equivalent`.

## `rflap_combine`

**Combine two machines** · shows the widget

Puts two machines of the same type side by side in one document (JFLAP's "Combine Automata"), ready to add λ-transitions for a union or concatenation. Example: {"a":{...fa...},"b":{...fa...}}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | object | yes | The first machine. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `b` | object | yes | The second machine. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |

`structuredContent` keys: `document`.

## `rflap_analyze`

**Analyze a machine**

Structure of an automaton: kind (dfa, nfa, dpda, npda, turing, mealy, moore), alphabet, deterministic?, nondeterministic states, λ transitions, unreachable and useless states, completeness. Example: {"document":{"type":"fa",...}}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | object | yes | The machine to analyze. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |

`structuredContent` keys: `alphabet`, `deterministic`, `kind`.

## `rflap_grammar`

**Check or transform a grammar** · shows the widget

With action `type` (default) classifies a grammar (regular / right_linear / left_linear / context_free / context_sensitive / unrestricted, CNF, GNF). Other actions transform it and return the new grammar: remove_lambda, remove_unit, remove_useless, cnf (Chomsky normal form), to_fa (right-linear grammar → automaton), to_pda_ll, to_pda_lr (CFG → PDA). Example: {"grammar":"S -> aSb | λ","action":"cnf"}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `type` \| `remove_lambda` \| `remove_unit` \| `remove_useless` \| `cnf` \| `to_fa` \| `to_pda_ll` \| `to_pda_lr` | no | What to do (default type). |
| `grammar` | string or object | yes | The grammar. Either the text, one production per line ("S -> aSb \| λ": an uppercase letter is a variable, anything else a terminal, λ is the empty string), or a grammar document. |

`structuredContent` keys: `classification`, `document`.

## `rflap_parse`

**Parse strings with a grammar** · shows the widget

Parses one or many strings: parser brute (default, any grammar), brute_unrestricted, ll1 (needs an LL(1) grammar), slr1, cyk (needs Chomsky normal form). Returns, per input, accepted / rejected, the leftmost derivation, the parse tree and the parser steps. A parser that cannot handle the grammar reports it per input. Example: {"grammar":"S -> aSb | λ","inputs":["aabb","aab"],"parser":"ll1"}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `budget` | integer | no | Candidate forms a brute-force search may examine per input (default 20000). |
| `grammar` | string or object | yes | The grammar. Either the text, one production per line ("S -> aSb \| λ": an uppercase letter is a variable, anything else a terminal, λ is the empty string), or a grammar document. |
| `input` | string | no | One string to parse. |
| `inputs` | array of string | no | Many strings to parse. |
| `parser` | `brute` \| `brute_unrestricted` \| `ll1` \| `slr1` \| `cyk` | no | The parser (default brute). |

`structuredContent` keys: `parser`, `results`.

## `rflap_parse_tables`

**FIRST/FOLLOW and parse tables** · shows the widget

FIRST and FOLLOW sets, the LL(1) table and the SLR(1) automaton with its ACTION/GOTO tables, with conflicts marked. The tool for "build the LL(1) table of this grammar". Example: {"grammar":"E -> TA\nA -> +TA | λ\nT -> i"}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grammar` | string or object | yes | The grammar. Either the text, one production per line ("S -> aSb \| λ": an uppercase letter is a variable, anything else a terminal, λ is the empty string), or a grammar document. |

`structuredContent` keys: `first`, `follow`, `ll1`, `slr1`.

## `rflap_render`

**Render a document** · shows the widget

Draws a document as svg (machines and L-systems), markdown (transition table), dot (Graphviz) or text. `highlight_states` (names) and `highlight_transitions` (indices from rflap_analyze) mark what you are explaining. Example: {"document":{...},"format":"markdown","highlight_states":["q1"]}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dark` | boolean | no | Dark theme. |
| `depth` | integer | no | Rewrite level when drawing an L-system (default 3). |
| `document` | object | yes | The document to draw. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `format` | `svg` \| `markdown` \| `dot` \| `text` | no | Output format (default svg). |
| `highlight_states` | array of string | no | State names to highlight. |
| `highlight_transitions` | array of integer | no | Transition indices to highlight. |

`structuredContent` keys: `content`, `document`, `format`.

## `rflap_open_jff`

**Open a JFLAP file** · shows the widget

Reads a JFLAP .jff file (any type) into a document and shows it. Pass the file's text as `xml`, or `path` to a file on the machine where this server runs (local use only).

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | Path of a .jff file to read (local servers only). |
| `xml` | string | no | The text of the .jff file. |

`structuredContent` keys: `document`.

## `rflap_save_jff`

**Save as a JFLAP file**

Writes a document as .jff text that JFLAP 7.1 opens. Returns the XML; with `path` (a .jff file on the machine where this server runs, local use only) it also writes the file, refusing to overwrite unless `overwrite` is true.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | object | yes | The document to save. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | Allow replacing an existing file. |
| `path` | string | no | Where to write the file; must end in .jff (local servers only). |

`structuredContent` keys: `type`, `xml`.

## `rflap_lsystem_render`

**Draw an L-system** · shows the widget

Expands an L-system `depth` levels (max 12) and draws it with the turtle. Example: {"document":{"type":"lsystem","axiom":"F","rules":["F -> F + F - F - F + F"],"parameters":{"angle":"90","distance":"4"}},"depth":2}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `depth` | integer | no | Rewrite level (default 3, at most 12). |
| `document` | object | yes | An lsystem document. A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `include_svg` | boolean | no | Put the SVG text in the reply as well (default false). |
| `options` | object | no | Drawing options: seed, ... (see rflap_capabilities). |

`structuredContent` keys: `depth`, `expansion_length`, `svg`.

## `rflap_pumping`

**Pumping lemma game** · shows the widget

JFLAP's pumping lemma games. action `languages` lists the 26 predefined languages; `new` starts a game (kind regular|context_free, language = index or title, mode human_first|computer_first); `move` plays one move on the `game` document that `new` returned: {"move":"choose_m","m":3}, {"move":"choose_w","w":"aabb"}, choose_decomposition, choose_i, add_case, ... Example: {"action":"new","kind":"regular","language":0,"mode":"computer_first"}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `languages` \| `new` \| `move` | yes | What to do. |
| `game` | object | no | The game document returned by `new` or `move` (move). A JSON object with a "type": fa, pda, turing, mealy, moore, grammar, regex, lsystem or a pumping lemma game. Compact form: {"type":"fa","initial":"q0","finals":["q1"], "transitions":[["q0","a","q1"]]}, {"type":"grammar","text":"S -> aSb \| λ"}, {"type":"regex","expression":"(a+b)*abb"}; the full form other tools return works too. Other types: rflap_capabilities. |
| `kind` | `regular` \| `context_free` | no | Which lemma (new). |
| `language` | integer or string | no | Index or title from `languages` (new). |
| `mode` | `human_first` \| `computer_first` | no | Who moves first (new). |
| `move` | object | no | The move, e.g. {"move":"choose_w","w":"aabb"} (move). |
| `seed` | integer | no | Seed of the computer's choices (new). |

## `rflap_capabilities`

**What Rflap can do**

The full description of the Rflap API: every operation with an example, every document type with its compact syntax, every conversion. Read it once when you need the exact syntax of a PDA, Turing machine, L-system… `section` narrows the reply.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `section` | `overview` \| `operations` \| `document_types` \| `convert` \| `all` | no | Which part (default overview). |

## `rflap_call`

**Raw Rflap API call**

Escape hatch: sends one raw Rflap API request {"op": ..., ...} (see rflap_capabilities) and returns the raw result. Use it for operations without a dedicated tool: normalize, layout, multiple_run, user_parse, explain, … Example: {"request":{"op":"layout","document":{...},"algorithm":"tree"}}.

| argument | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request` | object | yes | The request object; `op` names the operation. |
